title: Compact session credit economics — scratchpad
body:
Purpose
- Quick personal scratchpad to test a compact session-credit model that balances interactive UX and unit economics for low-to-medium usage customers. Not a proposal yet — just exploring numbers and tradeoffs.

Assumptions (starting point)
- Infra cost (amortized token-level): $0.60 per 1k input+output tokens (hosted, mixed models, average) — includes compute, mem, misc infra.
- Model/FP32-optimized variant price delta: quantized variant saves ~35% token cost.
- Average interactive session: 7 round trips, 150 tokens/user message, 200 tokens/model response. -> approx 7*(150+200)=2,450 tokens/session.
- Long tail sessions: 5% of sessions > 10k tokens; caching + KV cache reduces marginal cost for repeated prefixes by ~20%.
- Support & infra overhead (billing, logs, SLA): add $0.08 per session.

Base math (per-session)
- Tokens/session ~ 2.45k -> infra cost = 2.45 * $0.60 = $1.47
- Add support overhead = $0.08 -> total raw cost ~ $1.55
- Target gross margin (for starter/SMB tier) = 60% -> price per session ~ $3.88 (~$4)

Converting to credits
- Idea: sell "session credits" where 1 credit = 1 compact session baseline (2.45k tokens).
- Bulk packs: 100 credits, 1,000 credits, monthly subscriptions that include credits + optional SLOs.
- Price anchors: single credit price = $4 (as above) but bulk gives steep discounts:
  - 100 credits -> $320 (20% off) -> $3.20/credit
  - 1,000 credits -> $2,700 (32.5% off) -> $2.70/credit
  - Reserved monthly commit (2k credits/month) -> $2.25/credit (approx)

Edge cases & dynamic scaling
- Short micro-interactions (<= 200 tokens total): charge 0.25 credit to avoid overcharging tiny interactions.
- Very long sessions (> 10k tokens): bill in "credit chunks" where each additional 5k tokens beyond baseline = 2 credits (because caching helps reduce marginal cost).
- Model-swap premium: if customer uses high-capacity model or disables quantized variant, multiply credit cost by 1.6 for those calls.

Example customer scenarios
- Solo dev: 25 sessions/day -> ~750 sessions/month -> 750 * $4 = $3k/mo if bought ad-hoc credits (ouch). Bundled starter plan: 1,000 credits for $2.7k -> saves 10% and smooths spikes.
- SMB chat app (100 MAUs, moderate activity): assume 3 sessions/user/day -> 9k sessions/mo -> credits needed ~9k -> reserved 10k credits/month at $2.25 = $22.5k/mo (~$2.5/active session). Compare to raw payg: $36k/mo.
- Enterprise: huge variance, wants SLO + private deployment. Price via committed seat + reserved credits + per-API overage.

Unit-econ considerations (quick)
- CAC payback target: 3 months -> need gross margin and ARPU to support sales/CS costs. Starter plan must not be heavy-handed with credits unless it drives higher usage.
- Refund / unused credits policy: monthly expiration vs 12-month rollover affects recognized revenue and churn math. Prefer short expirations for free-tier.

Open questions / TODOs
- What is the right baseline token count? 2.45k assumed but product experiments may show median session is 900 tokens. Need to pull analytics. (Linked: CONFLUENCE-5682 request for per-route median tokens)
- How to express credits in UI to non-technical product managers? Need clear examples: "Starter pack = 400 short chats or 100 long research sessions"
- Overprovisioning and reserved capacity pricing: should reserved credits be tied to Dedicated capacity discounts for enterprise? Probably yes — align with Dedicated SKU pricing.
- Do we enable auto-quantization fallback to hit lower credit cost? UX/consent implications.

Operational / billing notes
- Charge per-session at time of completion to avoid dangling in-flight sessions. For long sessions, charge incremental chunks every X tokens (e.g., every 2.5k tokens).
- Add a lightweight metering header in API responses that includes credits consumed for transparency. (product ask)

Quick experiments to run
1) Pull 90-day token histogram by route and percentiles (p50/p90/p99).
2) Simulate price elasticity: run 3-day A/B with two credit pack prices for new signups.
3) Prototype UI text for credit consumption and ask research team for clarity test.

Random notes to self
- Maybe call single credit size "Compact Session" and make "Extended Session" = 3 credits. Names stick better than raw numbers.
- Keep micro-interactions cheap to encourage widget-style use (chat snippets).
- Need to bake in model substitution transparency for cost-sensitive customers.

References
- See shared drive pricing models for earlier back-of-envelope: (noted in CONFLUENCE-5682).
- Slack thread: #pricing-team 2024-12-03 discussed pack sizing.

End of scratchpad — will iterate when we get analytics.
